name: Aerospace Propulsion
description: Inspect, troubleshoot, repair and test aircraft engines and propulsion systems. This work combines mechanical reasoning, careful measurement and teamwork.
training: Basic Military Training, followed by propulsion technical training and supervised development in the specialty.
civilian: Aircraft maintenance, mechanical systems and technical inspection. Civilian aviation work may require additional FAA credentials.
project: With a teacher, compare how a classroom motor converts energy into motion. Make a labeled diagram and a maintenance checklist.
question: How is an engine specialty assigned, and which civilian maintenance credentials can this training support?

courses.why: Explore engines, energy and mechanical systems before studying aircraft propulsion.
Practice building, testing and improving a physical system.
Use formulas and measurements to reason about mechanical performance.
Extend mechanical troubleshooting after the introductory course.
Connect forces, motion and energy to how propulsion works.
Learn to interpret and communicate the shape of components.

portrait_direction: In the maintenance setting, contain long hair in a securely fastened compact bun, clear of tools and equipment. No loose hair, dangling jewelry or loose clothing near machinery. Show eye protection appropriate to the depicted workshop task. Preserve the reference identity while adapting grooming to the workplace.

name: Air Traffic Control
tagline: Bring clarity to a busy sky.
description: Help aircraft move safely on the ground and in the air using visual information, radar and precise communication.
training: Basic Military Training, air traffic control technical training and further qualification for assigned duties.
civilian: Air traffic services and aviation operations. Civilian controller hiring and certification have separate requirements.
project: Create a tabletop airport diagram and explain a fictional traffic sequence in clear, concise language. Use a classroom exercise, never a live aviation frequency.
question: What does qualification at a first duty station involve, and how does military experience relate to civilian controller requirements?

course_notes.Geometry: Build spatial reasoning for positions, directions and distances.
course_notes.Algebra II: Strengthen numerical reasoning and interpreting relationships.
course_notes.Physics I: Understand motion and the physical setting of flight.
course_notes.21st Century Communication: Organize information so other people can act on it.
course_notes.Exploration of Computer Science: Practice logical thinking and interpreting information in computer-based systems.
course_notes.Algebra I: Build foundational numerical reasoning; choose the next math level based on completed courses and placement.

portrait_direction: For the control-room setting, secure long hair in a neat low bun clear of the headset ear cushions, microphone and face. Do not copy loose hair over the shoulders from the student reference. Preserve hair color, texture and facial identity while changing the hairstyle. Show a correctly worn communications headset.

name: Pilot
tagline: Turn curiosity about flight into a plan.
description: Fly assigned aircraft and work with crews to carry out missions. Pilot selection and aircraft assignment are competitive and depend on qualifications, performance and Air Force needs.
training: Earn a bachelor’s degree and an officer commission through an eligible route; compete for pilot selection, meet aviation standards, then complete pilot and aircraft-specific training.
civilian: Commercial aviation, flight operations and aviation management. FAA certificates, flight experience and employer requirements apply.
project: Build and test paper gliders with one design change at a time. Graph the results and explain what the data can—and cannot—tell you.
question: Which commissioning routes fit my college plans, and what are the selection process, medical standards and service commitment for pilots?

courses.why: Develop the spatial reasoning used to understand flight paths.
Build the mathematical foundation for later quantitative study.
Connect motion, forces and energy to flight.
Prepare for college mathematics and technical coursework.
Practice concise briefings and communicating with a team.
Test design ideas and learn from measured results.

portrait_direction: Cockpit grooming and equipment: if the reference person has long hair, gather ALL of it into a compact, securely pinned low bun positioned clear of the headset. Keep the face, shoulders, chest, headset ear cushions and controls clear of loose hair. No loose lengths, tendrils or dangling ponytail. Hair may be restyled while preserving hair color, texture and recognizable facial identity. Show a correctly seated aviation headset in a generic parked aircraft cockpit or simulator. Keep clothing fitted and jewelry away from equipment; do not add military insignia or claim uniform compliance.

name: Developmental Engineer
tagline: Design the systems behind the mission.
description: Apply engineering to the development, evaluation and improvement of systems. Coordinate technical work and help assess new technologies.
training: Complete a qualifying engineering bachelor’s degree and an officer commissioning route. Specialty education and experience requirements must be confirmed with an officer recruiter.
civilian: Engineering design, systems engineering and technical project work. Roles and professional licensure may require additional qualifications.
project: Design a model wing or simple structure. Set a measurable goal, compare prototypes and document why you changed the design.
question: Which engineering degrees qualify, and how do technical specialties and commissioning routes affect selection?

courses.why: Practice an iterative design, build and test process.
Communicate technical ideas through drawings.
Connect mechanical, electrical and computing ideas.
Build a foundation in physical systems.
Prepare for the mathematics of an engineering degree.
Bring research and design together in a supervised project.

name: Cyber Systems Operations
description: Support servers and computer systems, maintain protective measures and respond to service interruptions.
training: Basic Military Training followed by technical and specialty training. Ask a recruiter about current cyber career names, codes and available assignments.
civilian: IT support, systems administration and cybersecurity operations. Certifications and employer requirements vary.
project: Create a diagram of a fictional school computer network and a backup-and-recovery plan. Work only with systems you own or are authorized to use.
question: Which current cyber specialty corresponds to this career page, and what training and certifications are available?

courses.why: Build foundations in computational thinking and computing systems.
Study algorithms, data and the wider impact of computing.
Practice creating and testing a working digital product.
Develop structured problem-solving skills.
Explain technical problems clearly to other people.
Practice diagnosing how software and hardware work together.

name: Aerospace Medical Service
tagline: Put care at the center of your work.
description: Support patient care, medical equipment and clinical teams. Duties can include treatment support and aeromedical evacuation responsibilities.
training: Basic Military Training followed by medical technical training and clinical development. This enlisted specialty is distinct from becoming a commissioned nurse or physician.
civilian: Patient-care support, allied health and further healthcare education. Civilian nursing or other licensed practice requires its own education and credentials.
project: Create a plain-language explanation of one body system using reputable health references. Ask a health-science teacher to review it.
question: What clinical training and credentials are included, and what additional education would I need for a civilian healthcare career?

courses.why: Build a foundation in living systems.
Connect body structures with their functions.
Understand chemical processes that underpin health science.
Learn the language used by clinical teams after Anatomy & Physiology.
Explore structured patient-care learning, subject to program requirements.
Develop understanding of behavior and human needs.

name: All Source Intelligence Analyst
description: Evaluate information from different sources and communicate analysis that helps leaders make informed decisions.
training: Basic Military Training followed by intelligence technical training. Confirm testing, citizenship, clearance and specialty requirements with a recruiter.
civilian: Research, data analysis and information-focused roles. Employers may require a degree, additional skills or a clearance.
project: Compare three public reports about the same nonmilitary event. Separate evidence from assumptions and give a short briefing with source links.
question: How much of the work involves writing, briefing and data analysis, and what qualifications are required for this specialty?

courses.why: Explore relationships among places, populations and human activity.
Interpret patterns while recognizing uncertainty.
Compare evidence and perspectives on current events.
Turn research into a clear briefing.
Build literacy in the tools used to organize information.
Explore another language and cultural context; choose the level that fits your prior learning.

name: Logistics Plans
description: Develop and review plans that coordinate operations, logistics and support organizations.
training: Basic Military Training followed by logistics technical training and development in planning duties.
civilian: Supply-chain planning, operations coordination and project support. Further education or certifications may be useful.
project: Plan the supplies and schedule for a fictional school event. Build a spreadsheet with quantities, costs, responsibilities and a contingency.
question: How do logistics planners work with other teams, and what analytical tools should I begin learning?

courses.why: Understand how organizations research and plan their work.
Practice accurate records and tracking resources.
Use data to think about demand and variation.
Build practical digital productivity skills.
Communicate a plan and answer questions.
Practice budgeting and evaluating trade-offs.

name: Security Forces
description: Help safeguard installations, people and resources through security and law-enforcement duties, incident response and reporting.
training: Basic Military Training followed by Security Forces technical training. Assignments can include demanding environments and deployment.
civilian: Public safety, security and emergency management. Civilian law-enforcement hiring, academies and licensing are separate.
project: With a teacher, review a fictional event-safety plan. Identify accessibility needs, communication responsibilities and where to seek adult help.
question: What does a typical first assignment involve, including schedules, deployment possibilities and further education?

courses.why: Explore the justice system and the responsibilities of public-safety work.
Consider behavior, communication and human needs.
Practice clear, respectful communication under pressure.
Learn how scientific evidence is observed and evaluated.
Build teamwork and healthy participation in physical activity.
Continue teamwork and physical education.
Develop sustainable personal fitness habits.

name: SERE Specialist
description: Train personnel to handle survival situations and support personnel-recovery preparation. SERE stands for Survival, Evasion, Resistance and Escape.
training: Basic Military Training, SERE orientation and specialist training. Selection includes demanding physical and other specialty standards.
civilian: Outdoor education, safety instruction and emergency-preparedness work. Civilian roles may require separate certifications.
project: Prepare a classroom lesson about weather awareness and safe trip planning. Have a qualified teacher review it; no solo survival exercises.
question: What are the current selection standards, training demands and day-to-day teaching responsibilities?

courses.why: Build an understanding of environments and ecological systems.
Explore hazards and preparedness.
Practice teaching and giving clear instructions.
Consider how people learn and respond to stress.
Develop teamwork and healthy physical activity habits.
Continue structured physical education.
Explore sustainable fitness and wellness planning.
